title: Matrix Density Waves and Fractionally Charged Point Defects in Flavor Weyl Semimetals
summary: A conventional interaction-driven Weyl density wave is a complex scalar and supports vortex lines, but no topologically stable point defects. We show that two Weyl flavors do not merely duplicate this order. Starting from the matrix-valued internode coherence, a local flavor-symmetric repulsion selects a traceless adjoint condensate within the density-wave sector, while the fermionic ground-state energy locks its complex components into the collinear form $\mathbfΔ=Φ_0\mathbf{n} e^{iθ}$.
